name: Rice wine
description: Fermented rice — drunk warm, and splashed into half of Chinese cooking.

tcm.note: Huang jiu is warm and moves qi and blood; it is used medicinally as a carrier for herbs.

histamine.note: Fermented, and worth flagging because it goes into so many dishes — the cooking does not remove the histamine.

guna.note: Aged, cured or fermented — the condition the texts call tamasic, whatever the ingredient started as.

effects.note: Alcohol measurably slows reaction time and narrows attention at ordinary drinking doses, well before intoxication feels subjectively obvious — one of the most consistently replicated findings in pharmacology, and the reason legal drink-driving limits exist at all. Drunk on its own rather than splashed into a wok, a cup delivers enough to produce it. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
